newsitem.title: UK: Brent softens a bit but other grades up on demand.
newsitem.headline: Brent softens a bit but other grades up on demand.

text.p: Brent crude seemed a little softer on Thursday in a quiet market but other North Sea grades gained a little due to continued good demand, traders said.
Two physical Brent cargoes traded on Thursday, one of them a second decade May at June Brent -37 cents compared with two Brents that changed hands at a 27 cents discount to June paper a day earlier.
Another Brent cargo loading May 14-16 fetched June Brent -25 cents.

"Brent is a little softer...but the picture in terms of margins and in terms of arbitrage with the United States is still good. I don't see at the moment any bad signs, though today was very quiet," one European trader said.
The May 14-16 cargo was bought by a U.S. refiner, the last cargo required to fill a Very Large Crude Carrier to the United States.
Activity was quiet due to holidays in most European countries, but other North Sea grades traded a litte higher.

A Forties cargo loading May 26-28 was sold by a European major at Dated Brent +23 cents -- three cents higher than a May 19-21 cargo that traded on Wednesday. A second May 17-19 Forties changed hands at a 20 cents premium to Dated.
A May 23 loading Ekofisk fetched Dated Brent +16 cents, also three cents higher from its last trading level on Tuesday.
"Seems that Oseberg is a little bit under pressure," one European buyer said.
